counterexamples.name: literal advisory HARD
counterexamples.finding: An exact source quotation plus a correctly reversed event pair still does not establish mandatory force. Guard returns temporal consistency, not semantic entailment or repair authorization.

counterexamples.name: benign paraphrase
counterexamples.finding: Exact-text matching rejects an equivalent paraphrase of an explicit mandatory order. It cannot be used as a general HARD semantic gate.

counterexamples.name: swapped witness roles
counterexamples.finding: Timestamp consistency cannot prove that requiredFirst/Second were correctly bound to the original source actions. Swapping the event roles can pass temporal consistency; the prototype never grants business repair authority.

recommendedScope: Keep original action requirements separate from newly inferred temporal relations; never weaken an original obligation merely because a derived order is unsupported.
Use program-captured original source as canonical evidence, not a mandatory literal-output match. Do not add independently blocking ORDER obligations merely from model MUST labels or numbered steps.

Require attributable complete same-task/session event pairs for confirmed historical order findings. Contradicted, external or unknown evidence is a checker/evidence issue, not a business-code repair.
Do not build a general natural-language modality classifier or shell-effect interpreter. No automatic rewriting of frozen historical baselines or budgets.
limits: Only deterministic replay and model-semantic probes; no new native Gateway, business development or full Stop loop in this round.
Current-policy text excerpts plus a shared experimental JSON contract are not an exact replica of the production multi-stage runtime.
Candidate 4/4 across one batch does not prove robustness; the scoped baseline timed out at 60 seconds.
Four API requests in total, no automatic retries. Initial invalid/confounded outputs retained.
Prototype does not authorize production HARD gates; semantic entailment and clause-to-action binding remain separate concerns.
Historical replay fixes action-to-event binding from already audited native calls; it does not validate autonomous model binding. The isolated guard must not directly become production authorization.
Prototype checks task/session only; production would also need the requirement applicability bound to the correct invocation/epoch, not arbitrary session history.
